# Appeal of Adverse Benefit Determination

**Member:** Avery Lawson
**Member ID:** W601208268
**Plan:** MedStar Family Choice DC (Commercial/ACA), District of Columbia
**Reference Number:** POC-0948C5760B-46622
**Date of Denial Notice:** 2026-08-06
**Governing Policy:** Utilization Management Criteria (https://www.medstarfamilychoicedc.com/-/media/project/mho/mfcdc/medical-policies-and-procedures/policy-115dc_utilization-management-criteria.pdf)

**RE: Appeal of denial of knee arthroscopy / meniscus surgery (CPT 29881)**

Dear MedStar Family Choice DC Appeals Department,

I am writing to request reconsideration of the denial of prior authorization for knee arthroscopy / meniscus surgery (CPT 29881), as stated in the notice dated 2026-08-06, reference number POC-0948C5760B-46622. My surgeon, Dr. Okafor, has documented that this procedure is medically necessary, and I am asking the plan to review that determination again.

## Why I believe this denial should be reversed

The denial states that "the imaging findings submitted do not support the medical necessity of the requested procedure." I do not believe this is accurate, based on the records already submitted with my prior authorization request.

My MRI, performed on 2026-05-28, shows a displaced bucket-handle tear of the medial meniscus with mechanical locking. My symptoms and function match this finding: I have had 24 months of progressive knee pain that is not relieved by rest, I experience locking and giving way, I cannot squat or kneel, and I am limited to walking on level surfaces. On examination, I had positive provocative testing on the affected side and pain-limited range of motion.

I have also already completed the conservative treatment that is typically expected before surgery is considered:

- **Physical therapy:** 16 weeks of supervised physical therapy focused on quadriceps strengthening and range of motion, with 20 visits completed between 2026-03-10 and 2026-06-30, as documented in my physical therapy discharge note.
- **Medication:** Six months of NSAIDs with inadequate relief.
- **Injection:** A corticosteroid injection on 2026-05-26, which gave only two weeks of partial relief.

I have no active infection and no untreated substance use, and I am a non-smoker.

## The plan has not shown me the specific clinical criteria it applied

The policy the denial cites, Utilization Management Criteria, states in general terms that:

> "This policy describes criteria utilized to facilitate consistency in Utilization Management (UM) decision making for medical and behavioral health requests."

> "MedStar Family Choice DC follows documented UM criteria to facilitate consistency in UM decision making across all service types."

> "All criteria utilized in utilization management are available upon request."

This language describes the plan's general process for utilization management decisions. It does not contain any specific clinical criteria for knee arthroscopy or meniscus surgery, and I have not been given the specific rule that my imaging and records supposedly failed to meet. Without that specific criterion in hand, I am not able to see exactly how the plan concluded that my MRI findings do not support medical necessity — and I do not believe the record supports that conclusion.

## Request for the specific criteria used

I understand that MedStar Family Choice DC may use InterQual criteria, which is licensed software rather than a publicly posted document. I am nonetheless entitled to see the specific criteria applied to my case. Under federal ERISA and ACA appeal rules, the plan must give me, free of charge, the specific rule or criterion it relied on to deny this request. I am formally requesting, in writing, **the InterQual subset, edition, and full criteria text applied to my determination**, so that I and my surgeon can respond to it directly.

## What I am asking for

1. That the plan reverse this denial and approve the knee arthroscopy / meniscus surgery (CPT 29881) as requested by Dr. Okafor.
2. That the plan provide, in writing, the specific InterQual subset, edition, and criteria text applied to my determination.
3. That the plan confirm receipt of this appeal.

I understand my appeal must be received by 2027-02-02. I am sending this appeal to the address printed on my denial letter; if that address is not clear, I will call the number on the back of my insurance card to confirm where member appeals are filed.

Please contact me if any additional information is needed to complete this review.

Sincerely,

Avery Lawson
Member ID: W601208268
Address: [patient mailing address]
Phone: [patient phone number]
Email: [patient email address]
Date: [date letter is sent]

---

*This letter is not medical or legal advice and does not guarantee that coverage will be approved.*
